title: Milloin: answering with everyday time expressions
summary: Milloin asks when something happens. Milloin sinä tulet? — Tulen huomenna.
targetSkills: Milloin: answering with everyday time expressions
objectives: Ask when an event happens with milloin.
Give an everyday time expression in a short or full reply.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern.
A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached.
A weak stem uses the changed consonants shown in the construction steps; the strong stem keeps the corresponding strong consonants.

Milloin asks when something happens. Put it before the supplied clause: Milloin sinä tulet? (“When are you coming?”). Present-tense Finnish can describe a planned future event when a time word makes the meaning clear.
keyPoints: Milloin asks about time, not place or reason.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Answer with a time expression such as tänään (“today”), huomenna (“tomorrow”), nyt (“now”), aamulla (“in the morning”) or illalla (“in the evening”). These taught expressions are learned as complete forms. A full reply includes the appropriate verb; a short time expression also answers milloin.
A natural short reply to “Milloin sinä tulet?” is “Huomenna.” (“Tomorrow.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
Reject an incorrect time and state the actual time. The complete negative phrase en tule is provided; the time expressions stay unchanged.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Supply the requested time rather than a yes/no answer.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: aamulla means in the morning here. Aamu + -lla gives the conventional time expression aamulla.
illalla means in the evening here. Ilta changes lt to ll and adds -lla: illalla.

tulet: you come; verb (the action or state). Use the stem tule- and singular second-person -t: tulet.
Tulen: I come; verb (the action or state). Tulla removes -la and adds e to form tule-, then adds -n: tulen.
huomenna: tomorrow; time. Huomenna is a complete time expression meaning tomorrow.

steps: En: I do not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). En is the first-person singular negative verb. The main verb takes its negative form.
tule: come; main verb after the negative verb. Remove -n from tulen to obtain the negative main-verb form tule; the negative verb carries the person.
